extracted text: The material was aeronautical, 2024 aluminum alloy in T351 temper, which is used in aircraft applications due to its high specific strength properties and good damage tolerance behavior. The T351 temper includes solid solution heat treatment, cold work and natural aging. The panels had a thickness of 3.2 mm and 15 mm for the sheet and plate material respectively. Mechanical properties from Table 2 show that the plate material exhibits slightly higher values of yield and tensile strength compared to the sheet material. The plate material has lower elongation to fracture and higher critical stress intensity factor than the sheet.
property mapping:
Yield Strength (ΜPa) = YS [MPa]
Tensile Strength (ΜPa) = UTS [MPa]
Elongation to fracture, A50 (%) = elong [%]
Critical stress intensity factor (at crack length Δα = 40 mm), Kcr (ΜPa m1/2) = fracture toughness
abbreviations:
ppm = parts per million (used for trace elements like Cr, Zr, and Pb)
T351 = temper condition that includes solution heat treatment, cold work, and natural aging
